query: A Hard Frost {A hard frost is coming down out of a clear sky. Old Maud is going along the row of clay smudge pots under the humming pear with a tinderbox that won't strike. "Every one, dearie," she says, "or the old pear sulks for a month."|Frost again. The pear has gone quiet, which Maud says is how it shivers.|The smudge pots are set out before you arrive. Maud has left a second tinderbox on the wall, for you.} Light the pots with a tinderbox {Forty pots, a tinderbox and numb fingers. The last one catches as the frost comes down, and the pear starts humming again, low and grateful.|You light pot after pot on your knees in the frost. Maud brings you something hot in a chipped cup and doesn't say what it is.|You light your half of the row before Maud lights hers, and she pretends to be cross about it.} Wrap the low branches in sacking {You climb into the lower branches and wrap what you can reach. It isn't all of it. Maud says some is a lot more than none.|Sacking, string and a ladder that leans the wrong way. You save the low branches; the top will have to take its chances.|You wrap the branches like presents. Maud says the pear will remember, and she says it as if pears do.} Light every pot at once {You hold out your hand and every pot in the row blooms at once, a line of small suns in the frost. Maud laughs, which you've never heard her do so loudly.|One breath, forty flames. The pear hums so loudly the bees come out to see. "Well," says Maud. "Aren't you handy."|{spell_level(flame) >= 3: You light the pots and hold the warmth over the whole tree like a hand. Not one bud browns. Maud says she'll name a pear after you, and does.|You light the row in two breaths. Maud says it took her forty years to learn to do it with a tinderbox, and she isn't sure which of you to be proud of.}}
